name: Cuba
summary: A Spanish colony until 1898, independent in 1902; Fidel Castro’s revolution (1959) made it a communist state; the 1962 missile crisis brought the world close to nuclear war.

knownFor.label: Havana Old Town
knownFor.note: Colonial city and old American cars.

knownFor.label: Cuban music
knownFor.note: Son, salsa, Buena Vista Social Club.

location.value: The largest country in the Caribbean by area; officially about 109,884 km².

terrain.value: Mostly flat to rolling plains, with the Sierra Maestra mountains in the south-east.

climate.value: Tropical, with a drier season (November–April) and a rainier season (May–October).

resources.value: Sugar, tobacco, fish, citrus fruits and coffee; nickel is the most important mineral.

disasters.value: Frequent hurricanes, most common in September and October.

population.value: 11.2 million at the 2010 census; the population has been falling since 2006.

urbanisation.value: Havana is the capital and largest city.

disease.value: Free universal health care, though with shortages of drugs and equipment; tens of thousands of medical staff work abroad.

migration.value: Large emigration since the 1959 revolution has created a big diaspora; the United States is the top destination.

economicBase.value: A command economy dominated by tourism and exports of skilled labour, sugar, tobacco and coffee.

wealth.value: Shortages and poverty in recent years.

moneyAndTax.value: The Cuban peso (CUP), the only currency since 2021.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A one-party socialist state led by the Communist Party.

keyRulers.value: José Martí. Fulgencio Batista. Fidel Castro. Raúl Castro.

succession.value: The National Assembly elects the president; the Communist Party’s First Secretary is the most powerful post.

institutions.value: The Communist Party and the 470-member National Assembly of People’s Power.

stability.value: Revolution (1959); large protests against the government (July 2021).

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The Revolutionary Armed Forces; during the Cold War the largest armed forces per person in Latin America, equipped by the Soviet Union.

majorWars.value: War of Independence (1895–98); revolution; Bay of Pigs (1961); troops in Angola.

alliancesRivals.value: Backed by the Soviet Union during the Cold War; long in conflict with the United States.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: A literacy rate of 99.8% thanks to free education; the University of Havana was founded in 1728.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

religion.value: Mainly Christian, often mixed with Santería, and many non-religious; the state stopped calling itself atheist in 1992.

artsArchitecture.value: Music such as son, the basis of mambo, cha-cha-chá and salsa; Spanish colonial architecture.

socialStructure.value: A multiethnic population of Spanish, African and Taíno descent, with much mixed ancestry.

sharedIdentity.value: José Martí is the national hero, and the constitution is guided by his ideas and those of Marx, Engels and Lenin.

dailyLife.value: Black beans and rice (moros y cristianos) and plantains are staples; food is rationed.

ideasReligions.value: Cuba supported revolutionary movements across Africa and Latin America from the 1960s to the 1980s.

colonisation.value: Part of the Spanish Empire until 1898.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
